findings.issue: Source: "I would have gladly camped by the ships in the hope of taking them" (conditional, a past willingness). Candidate: "I gladly camped by the ships, hoping to take them" states it as a fact that Polydamas did camp.
findings.fix: “Think carefully, my friends. I urge you to go back to your city now and not wait here by the ships until morning, for we are far from our walls. As long as this man was at enmity with Agamemnon, the Achaeans were easier to deal with, and I would gladly have camped by the ships, hoping to take them. But now I am in great fear of the swift son of Peleus. He is so daring that he will never wait here on the plain, where Trojans and Achaeans fight with equal valor. He will try to storm our city and carry off our women. So do as I say, and let us retreat. This is what will happen. The darkness of night will hold the son of Peleus back for a while. But if he finds us here in the morning when he sallies out in full armor, we shall come to know him in good earnest. Glad will be the man who can escape and get back to Ilium, and many a Trojan will become meat for dogs and vultures—may I never live to hear it. If we do as I say, little as we may like it, we shall have strength in counsel during the night, and the great gates with the doors that close them will protect the city. At dawn we can arm and take our stand on the walls. He will regret it then if he sallies from the ships to fight us. He will go back when he has let his horses run their fill, driven in every direction under our walls, and he will have no mind to try to force his way into the city. Nor will he ever sack it. The dogs will devour him first.”

findings.issue: Beacon simile: "in case they may come with their ships and help them" leaves the subject of "they" (the neighbors) unclear; Butler's "if so be that they may come with their ships and succour them" has the same looseness.
Source: "which the gods gave to Peleus when they laid you in the couch of a mortal man"; candidate: "on the day they laid you in the bed". "On the day" is a slight narrowing of "when".
